Project Title: Enhanced understanding of air-sea interactions in the stable marine boundary layer and improving atmospheric river predictions in support of NOAA/OAR's Western Water Program

Project Description: The proposed work will build upon existing collaborative research and focus on an investigation of the MYNN PBL scheme's ability to represent near-surface exchange processes for the SMBL in AR environments. In addition to the dynamical model research, CW3E will collaborate with NOAA to develop AI modeling forecast capabilities for ARs over the Western United States by leveraging archived atmospheric reforecast datasets. Project Title: Advancing the prediction of Atmospheric Rivers via data assimilation, physics, and machine learning
Project Goal: The overall proposal goal is to improve the prediction of landfalling AR events in terms of precipitation type, timing, duration, and location. For the improvement of AR-AFS, GSL will contribute with physics innovations and testing. For MPAS-AR, improvements will be accomplished through optimal use of additional observation types in the DA system and evaluation of their relative importance, development of ensemble-based DA and forecasts, and development and coupling of physics parameterizations for the complex problem of predicting long-distance vapor transport and long-duration terrain-forced precipitation processes. We will continue our collaboration with PSL on deep cumulus parameterization development and testing. In addition to physical model approaches to AR prediction, this proposal includes the use of an AI-based model to explore the possibility of leveraging it to increase AR predictability.
Research Keywords: Model & Forecast Guidance, Water in the West
Associated Forecast Systems & Models: Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS), Unified Forecast System (UFS)
Project Description: For all three main areas (MPAS-AR, AR-AFS, and data-driven Models), the technical approach to achieve the major outcomes will be to develop and apply science-based enhancements and/or new procedures, then test and refine procedures based on qualitative and quantitative assessments of results, followed by transition of the enhancements to the end-to-end modeling systems.
Project Benefits: Development and testing of AR-AFS will contribute to a high-readiness on-demand system that can be deployed by the NWS in real time to create additional guidance in case of AR events. Development and further enhancements to the MPAS-AR prototype forecast system, including its scale-aware physics, JEDI-based DA, and stochastic components, will lead to improved AR forecast skill for both large- and small-scale features at longer lead times. In addition, the development of high-resolution regional and variable-resolution global / regional ensemble forecast components to MPAS-AR will allow for the improved characterization of forecast uncertainty, which will be very beneficial to emergency managers and other officials tasked with making critical water-related decisions with differing lead-time constraints. Furthermore, the development of an AI-based model component will augment traditional ensemble formulations, allowing potential further increases in both forecast skill and forecast uncertainty characterization. Datasets from these forecast components will also be beneficial to researchers examining methods for creating optimal decision support tools.

Project Title: Advancing the prediction of atmospheric rivers via enhanced physics parameterizations, data assimilation, and machine-learning models
Project Goal: The project has two main goals further develop a regional data-driven ensemble system for atmospheric river prediction and further develop a series of prototype MPAS-based atmospheric river forecast systems, dubbed MPAS-AR, with three supporting major objectives. 1) Develop more sophisticated physics parameterizations. 2) Advance ensemble prediction capabilities. and 3) Advance JEDI-based hourly cycled data assimilation (DA) capabilities.
